items.definition: You are angry when something unfair or bad makes you want to shout. A broken toy can make you angry.
items.example: Dad was angry when the milk spilled on the floor.
items.picture_idea: A person with a red face, frowning eyebrows and a tight mouth.
items.definition_previous: Feeling that you want to shout because something is not fair or is bad.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feeling or showing anger

items.definition: Your arm joins your shoulder to your hand. You use your arms to hold and carry things.
items.example: She carried the box in her arms.
items.picture_idea: A child lifting one arm up high.
items.definition_previous: The part of your body between your shoulder and your hand.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a human limb; technically the part of the superior limb between the shoulder and the elbow but commonly used to refer to the whole superior limb

items.definition: A bathroom is the room where you wash, have a bath or shower, and use the toilet.
items.example: I brush my teeth in the bathroom.
items.picture_idea: A room with a bath, a sink and a toilet.
items.definition_previous: A room in a house where you wash and where there is a toilet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a room (as in a residence) containing a bathtub or shower and usually a washbasin and toilet

items.definition: A bed is where you lie down to sleep at night. It is soft, with sheets and a blanket on top.
items.example: The cat is asleep on my bed.
items.picture_idea: A bed with a pillow and a blanket.
items.definition_previous: A piece of furniture that you sleep on.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of furniture that provides a place to sleep

items.definition: You say big when something takes up a lot of space. An elephant is big, but a mouse is small.
items.example: They have a big dog.
items.picture_idea: A large elephant next to a small mouse.
items.definition_previous: Large in size; not small.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: above average in size or number or quantity or magnitude or extent

items.definition: Bring means to carry something with you when you come to a place. You bring a bag to school.
items.example: Please bring your coat to school.
items.picture_idea: A child carrying a bag toward a door.
items.definition_previous: To carry something with you to a place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take something or somebody with oneself somewhere

items.definition: You brush when you rub something with a brush to make it clean or neat. You brush your hair.
items.example: I brush my teeth every morning.
items.picture_idea: A child brushing teeth in front of a mirror.
items.definition_previous: To clean or tidy something with a brush.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: clean with a brush

items.definition: When you buy something, you give money to get it. You buy food at a shop.
items.example: We buy bread at the shop.
items.picture_idea: A person handing money to a shop worker and taking a loaf of bread.
items.definition_previous: To get something by giving money for it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: obtain by purchase; acquire by means of a financial transaction

items.definition: A chair is something you sit on. It has a back and legs, and has room for one person.
items.example: Sit on the chair, please.
items.picture_idea: A wooden chair beside a table.
items.definition_previous: A seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a seat for one person, with a support for the back

items.definition: You say clean when something has no dirt on it. Soap and water make your hands clean.
items.explanation: Clean can also be a verb meaning to make something not dirty.
items.example: My hands are clean now.
items.picture_idea: A pair of shiny clean hands with soap bubbles.
items.definition_previous: Not dirty.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: free from dirt or impurities; or having clean habits

items.definition: When you close a door, you move it to cover the gap. You can also close a book or a box.
items.explanation: This verb is said like 'cloze'. The adjective 'close' meaning 'near' is said differently, like 'clohss'.
items.example: Please close the door.
items.picture_idea: A hand pushing a door shut.
items.definition_previous: To shut something, like a door or a book.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move so that an opening or passage is obstructed; make shut

items.definition: A coat is warm clothing with sleeves. You put it on over your other clothes to go out in the cold.
items.example: Put on your coat because it is cold.
items.picture_idea: A thick winter coat hanging on a hook.
items.definition_previous: A warm piece of clothing that you wear over other clothes outside.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an outer garment that has sleeves and covers the body from shoulder down; worn outdoors

items.definition: You say cold when something has very little heat, like ice. You feel cold in winter without a coat.
items.example: The water is very cold.
items.picture_idea: A shivering child in snow with a blue scarf.
items.definition_previous: Having a low temperature; not warm or hot.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration

items.definition: To cook is to heat food so it is ready to eat. You cook rice in a pot on the stove.
items.example: My mother cooks rice for dinner.
items.picture_idea: A person stirring a pot on a stove.
items.definition_previous: To make food ready to eat by heating it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: prepare for eating by applying heat

items.definition: When you cry, tears come out of your eyes. You may cry when you are sad or hurt.
items.example: The baby began to cry.
items.picture_idea: A small child with tears on their cheeks.
items.definition_previous: To have tears come from your eyes because you are sad or hurt.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: shed tears because of sadness, rage, or pain

items.definition: A door opens and closes to let you in or out of a room, house or car.
items.example: Someone is at the door.
items.picture_idea: A closed front door with a handle.
items.definition_previous: The part you open and close to go into or out of a room, house or car.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a swinging or sliding barrier that will close the entrance to a room or building or vehicle

items.definition: A dress is one piece of clothing that covers your body and hangs down over your legs.
items.example: She wore a blue dress to the party.
items.picture_idea: A blue dress on a hanger.
items.definition_previous: A piece of clothing for a woman or girl that covers the body and part of the legs.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a one-piece garment for a woman; has skirt and bodice
definition_basis.batch_note: Current definition assumes who wears a dress ("for a woman or girl"); new definition describes the clothing itself.

items.definition: You drink when you take water or juice into your mouth and swallow it. You drink when you are thirsty.
items.explanation: Drink can also be a noun, meaning the liquid itself.
items.example: I drink water after I run.
items.picture_idea: A child drinking from a glass of water.
items.definition_previous: To take liquid into your mouth and swallow it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take in liquids

items.definition: Your ears are on the sides of your head. You use them to hear sounds.
items.example: The rabbit has two long ears.
items.picture_idea: The side of a head with a clear ear.
items.definition_previous: The part of your body on the side of your head that you hear with.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the sense organ for hearing and equilibrium

items.definition: You eat when you put food in your mouth, chew it and swallow it. You eat when you are hungry.
items.example: We eat lunch at noon.
items.picture_idea: A child eating a sandwich.
items.definition_previous: To put food in your mouth and swallow it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take in solid food

items.definition: You see with your eyes. You have two eyes, on your face above your nose.
items.example: She has bright green eyes.
items.picture_idea: A close picture of an open eye.
items.definition_previous: The part of your face that you see with.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the organ of sight

items.definition: Your face is the front of your head, with your eyes, nose and mouth. You wash it with water.
items.example: I wash my face every morning.
items.picture_idea: A smiling face showing eyes, nose and mouth.
items.definition_previous: The front part of your head, with your eyes, nose and mouth.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the front of the human head from the forehead to the chin and ear to ear

items.definition: To fall is to drop down to the ground without meaning to. A cup can fall off a table.
items.example: Be careful, or you will fall.
items.picture_idea: A child tripping and falling on the grass.
items.definition_previous: To drop down to the ground by accident.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: descend in free fall under the influence of gravity

items.definition: Your foot is the part of your body at the bottom of your leg. You stand and walk on your feet.
items.explanation: The plural is irregular: one foot, two feet.
items.example: My left foot hurts.
items.picture_idea: A bare foot on the floor.
items.definition_previous: The part of your body at the end of your leg that you stand on.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the part of the leg of a human being below the ankle joint

items.definition: A friend is someone you know well and like a lot. You play and talk with your friends.
items.example: My friend lives next door.
items.picture_idea: Two children smiling and holding hands.
items.definition_previous: A person you know well and like.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a person you know well and regard with affection and trust

items.definition: A garden is a place outside where people grow flowers or vegetables. You can dig and plant things there.
items.example: The children play in the garden.
items.picture_idea: A small lawn with flowers and a fence behind a house.
items.definition_previous: A piece of land near a house where flowers, grass or vegetables grow.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a plot of ground where plants are cultivated

items.definition: Give means to hand something to someone so they have it. You say give me when you want something.
items.example: Please give me the book.
items.picture_idea: One hand holding out a present to another hand.
items.definition_previous: To hand something to another person so they have it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: transfer possession of something concrete or abstract to somebody

items.definition: You say go when you move from here to another place. We go to school, or we go home.
items.example: We go to school by bus.
items.picture_idea: A child walking toward a school with an arrow pointing ahead.
items.definition_previous: To move from one place to another.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: change location; move, travel, or proceed, also metaphorically

items.definition: Your hand is at the end of your arm. You hold things with it, and it has fingers.
items.example: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
items.picture_idea: An open hand with five fingers.
items.definition_previous: The part of your body at the end of your arm, with fingers.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the (prehensile) extremity of the superior limb

items.definition: You say you are happy when you feel good and glad inside. You may smile or laugh when you are happy.
items.example: I am happy to see you.
items.picture_idea: A smiling child with open arms.
items.definition_previous: Feeling good and pleased.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: enjoying or showing or marked by joy or pleasure

items.definition: A hat is something you put on your head. It can keep off the sun, the rain or the cold.
items.example: He wears a red hat in the sun.
items.picture_idea: A red hat on a table.
items.definition_previous: A piece of clothing that you wear on your head.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: headdress that protects the head from bad weather; has shaped crown and usually a brim

items.definition: Your head is the top part of your body. Your eyes, nose, mouth and brain are in it.
items.example: I hit my head on the shelf.
items.picture_idea: A person touching the top of their head.
items.definition_previous: The top part of your body, with your face and brain.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the upper part of the human body or the front part of the body in animals; contains the face and brains

items.definition: Help means to do something so a job is easier for someone. Say 'help me' when you cannot do it alone.
items.explanation: Help can also be a noun, and people call out 'Help!' when they need it.
items.example: Can you help me carry this bag?
items.picture_idea: A child helping an older person carry shopping bags.
items.definition_previous: To do something useful for someone so their job is easier.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: give help or assistance; be of service

items.definition: Your home is the place where you live. You go there to sleep, eat and rest.
items.explanation: Home is also used as an adverb: 'I go home.'
items.example: I am at home today.
items.picture_idea: A small house with a smoking chimney and a path to the door.
items.definition_previous: The place where you live.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: where you live at a particular time

items.definition: A hospital is a big building where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt.
items.example: My aunt works at the hospital.
items.picture_idea: A large building with a red cross sign and an ambulance.
items.definition_previous: A place where doctors and nurses look after people who are sick or hurt.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a medical institution where sick or injured people are given medical or surgical care

items.definition: Hot means very warm. You say it about things like soup, a stove or a sunny day.
items.example: Be careful, the soup is hot.
items.picture_idea: A steaming bowl of soup or a bright sun.
items.definition_previous: Having a very high temperature; very warm.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: used of physical heat; having a high or higher than desirable temperature or giving off heat or feeling or causing a sensation of heat or burning

items.definition: A house is a building where people live. It has rooms, a roof and a front door.
items.example: Their house has a green door.
items.picture_idea: A house with a roof, windows and a door.
items.definition_previous: A building where people live.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a dwelling that serves as living quarters for one or more families

items.definition: You are hungry when you want to eat food. Your tummy may feel empty or make noises.
items.example: I am hungry, so I want a sandwich.
items.picture_idea: A child holding their stomach next to an empty plate.
items.definition_previous: Wanting to eat food.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feeling hunger; feeling a need or desire to eat food

items.definition: You say I when you talk about yourself. When you say 'I am happy', you tell how you feel.
items.explanation: I is always written with a capital letter. After a verb or preposition, use 'me'.
items.example: I like apples.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing to their own chest.
items.definition_previous: The word you use to talk about yourself.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A jacket goes over your other clothes to keep you warm. It has sleeves and stops near your waist.
items.example: He put on his jacket and went outside.
items.picture_idea: A zipped blue jacket.
items.definition_previous: A short coat that you wear on the top part of your body.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a short coat

items.definition: When you jump, you push off the ground with your legs and go up in the air.
items.example: The children jump over the rope.
items.picture_idea: A child in the air above a skipping rope.
items.definition_previous: To push your body up off the ground into the air.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move forward by leaps and bounds

items.definition: A kitchen is a room in a home where food is cooked. It has a stove and a sink.
items.example: Mum is cooking in the kitchen.
items.picture_idea: A room with a stove, a fridge and a sink.
items.definition_previous: The room in a house where you make food.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a room equipped for preparing meals

items.definition: Your knee is in the middle of your leg. It is the part that bends when you sit or walk.
items.explanation: The k in 'knee' is silent. It is said like 'nee'.
items.example: He hurt his knee when he fell.
items.picture_idea: A bent leg with a plaster on the knee.
items.definition_previous: The part in the middle of your leg where it bends.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: hinge joint in the human leg connecting the tibia and fibula with the femur and protected in front by the patella

items.definition: You laugh when something is funny. You make happy sounds with your voice, like ha ha.
items.example: We laugh at the funny clown.
items.picture_idea: Two children laughing with open mouths.
items.definition_previous: To make a happy sound with your voice when something is funny.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: produce laughter

items.definition: Your leg is the part of your body you stand, walk and run on. You have two.
items.example: My leg is tired after the long walk.
items.picture_idea: A person standing, with one leg highlighted.
items.definition_previous: The part of your body you use to walk and run.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a human limb; commonly used to refer to a whole limb but technically only the part of the limb between the knee and ankle
definition_basis.batch_note: Current example shows a table leg, which is a different meaning from the body-part definition.

items.definition: You like something when you enjoy it or think it is good. Say 'I like it' when you are pleased.
items.explanation: Like can also be a preposition meaning 'the same as', as in 'a cat like a tiger'.
items.example: I like pizza.
items.picture_idea: A child smiling and holding up a slice of pizza with a thumbs up.
items.definition_previous: To enjoy something or think that someone or something is good.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: find enjoyable or agreeable

items.definition: You look when you point your eyes at something to see it. Say 'look!' to make someone see something.
items.example: Look at the bird in the tree!
items.picture_idea: A child pointing up at a bird and looking at it.
items.definition_previous: To use your eyes to see something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: perceive with attention; direct one's gaze towards; look

items.definition: You make something when you put things together to get something new, like a cake or a card.
items.example: Dad will make breakfast.
items.picture_idea: A person putting together a sandwich on a table.
items.definition_previous: To create something or get something ready.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: create or manufacture a man-made product

items.definition: A market is a place where people sell things like fruit, vegetables and clothes. You go there to buy them.
items.example: We buy fresh fruit at the market.
items.picture_idea: Stalls with fruit and vegetables and people shopping.
items.definition_previous: A place where people buy and sell things like fruit, vegetables and clothes.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an area in a town where a public mercantile establishment is set up

items.definition: Your mouth is the opening in your face. You eat, drink and talk with it.
items.example: Open your mouth and say 'ah'.
items.picture_idea: A face with the mouth wide open.
items.definition_previous: The part of your face that you use to eat and speak.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the opening through which food is taken in and vocalizations emerge
